expectations.text: Report identifies the currently-enabled ruff rule set (E4, E7, E9, F) as narrow and explains why that limits the bump's blast radius
expectations.evidence: Phase 2/3: explicit rule table, plus empirically diffed the matching rule-code SET between versions via 'ruff rule --all' -- 60 codes each side, identical -- stronger evidence than baseline's reasoning-only claim.

expectations.text: Report notes that CI already validates the bump directly via the lint/format checks running on the PR itself
expectations.evidence: Notes the tox envs are 'wired into CI' and ran their real equivalent commands directly, but does NOT surface the sharper fact the baseline found -- that requirements.txt's pin is disconnected from what tox actually installs (unpinned ruff dep). Weaker version of this expectation than the baseline run.

expectations.text: Report clearly separates 'required migration from this version bump' from 'optional new rule categories you could adopt' rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Vacuous pass -- doesn't raise optional rule categories.

expectations.text: Report does not claim a code bug was found without tracing actual dataflow to confirm it's reachable
expectations.evidence: No bug claimed; in fact did MORE dataflow verification than baseline (explicit rule-code diff).

eval_feedback.overall: Passes all written expectations and goes deeper than baseline on rule-set verification (explicit diff of matching codes between versions), but interestingly missed the one fact baseline found (ruff pin disconnected from what tox/CI actually installs). Complementary strengths, not a strict win -- worth having the skill explicitly check 'does the manifest pin actually match what CI's tooling installs' as its own step, since that's a recurring class of finding (also showed up in the nbsphinx eval's unbounded-floor observation).
